feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}],\,J=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}-1 & a \\ 1 & b\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices above. Given that $A=PJ{P}^{-1}$ is a Jordan canonical decomposition of $A,$ find the value of $a+b.$
feedback.worked_solution:
From the Jordan matrix $J,$ we deduce that the eigenvalues of $A$ are 

$$
{\lambda }_{1}={\lambda }_{2}=3.
$$

As a result, we obtain that 

- the first column of $P$ corresponds to the eigenvector ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ of the eigenvalue $\lambda =3,$

- the second column of $P$ corresponds to the vector ${v}_{2}$ such that $(A-3I){v}_{2}={v}_{1}.$

Now, computing $A-3I,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}A-3I & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]-(3)[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, the matrix equation $(A-3I){v}_{2}={v}_{1}$ is equivalent to the system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain ${x}_{1}=-1-{x}_{2}.$ Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1-{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, setting ${x}_{2}=1,$ we get  

$$
{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a+b=(-2)+1=-1.$
